# hanzo-kernel

**Write a GPU kernel once in Rust. Run it on CUDA, ROCm, Vulkan, Metal, WebGPU, and CPU — at or above hand-tuned speed.**

```
use *;
```
That is the whole kernel. It lowers to native SPIR-V, PTX, HIP, and MSL — no per-backend rewrite, no shading-language dialect, no `unsafe` FFI.

## Why

A production inference stack hand-writes the same ~20 operations four times — once per backend, in four languages (CUDA C++, Metal Shading Language, HIP C++, GLSL). That Cartesian product isn't just a maintenance tax; it is where the bugs breed, because **one operation with four implementations has four numeric behaviors.** A model that generates coherently on Metal can collapse into repetition on CUDA — same weights, same math, different rounding in a hand-tuned kernel.

`hanzo-kernel` collapses the **product** into a **sum**: `backends × types × ops` → `backends + types + ops`. One Rust source per operation, lowered everywhere. Uniform numeric behavior stops being something you chase with four test suites and becomes a structural property of a single source.

## The claim, measured

Portability usually means a performance downgrade. It doesn't here. Every number below is measured, bit-exact-gated against a CPU oracle, and reproducible with the bundled `matvec-check` binary.

| Kernel | Backend | Result |
|---|---|---|
| int8 dp4a matvec | Vulkan (AMD gfx1151) | 196 GB/s — 118% of the hand-tuned kernel it replaces |
| int8 dp4a matvec | Metal (Apple M4 Max) | 206 GB/s |
| `rms_norm` | Vulkan, in the live engine | 10.6× the hand-written kernelit replaced (now deleted) |
| `softmax` | Vulkan, in the live engine | 351 GB/s (replaced the hand-written kernel) |
| all ops | CPU / Vulkan / Metal | bit-exact from one source(max_rel ≤ 1e-3) |

The `dot` on a `Line<i8>` lowers to a single `OpSDot` on Vulkan (verified in the emitted SPIR-V binary) — the *same* hardware integer-dot instruction the hand-written kernels use, 2.35× a scalar loop. The DSL doesn't emulate the fast path; it reaches it.

## Install

```
[]
 = "0.2"
```
Pick your backend with a feature flag (drop `cpu` for GPU-only builds — it pulls an LLVM/MLIR toolchain):

```
# GPU-only, no CPU toolchain
 = {  = "0.2",  = false,  = ["vulkan"] }
```
| Feature | Backend |
|---|---|
| `cpu`(default) | CPU reference runtime — the bit-exact oracle |
| `vulkan` | Vulkan (SPIR-V) — AMD, Intel, NVIDIA |
| `metal` | Metal (MSL) — Apple Silicon |
| `cuda` | CUDA (PTX/NVRTC) — NVIDIA |
| `rocm` | ROCm (HIP) — AMD |

## The surface

Three attributes and two nouns — named for what they are, not for a framework.

- `#[kernel(targets(...))]`— a launch entry point.- `targets(...)`is validated at compile time (an unknown backend is a compile error) and self-documents where the kernel runs.
- `#[device]`— an on-GPU helper function, inlined into a kernel. A kernel is- *launched*; a device function is a- *piece*of one.
- `Grid`/- `Block`— the launch shape: the grid of thread blocks, and the block of threads.
- `Array`,- `Float`,- `Line`— the data. Already the simple, accurate words.

Every performance primitive is a first-class part of the surface and lowers to the native instruction:

| Primitive | Lowers to |
|---|---|
| `Line<i8>::dot` | `dp4a`/`OpSDotAccSat`(int8 4-way dot) |
| `cmma` | tensor cores (WMMA / cooperative-matrix / simdgroup) |
| `plane_sum`,`plane_broadcast` | subgroup / warp reduce & shuffle |
| `SharedMemory`,`Atomic`, barriers | native shared memory, atomics, sync |

## Built-in op library

Reusable, bit-exact kernels — not toys. Each ships with a CPU oracle and a bit-exact gate.

- `quant`- `matvec_q8`,- `matvec_q4k`(in-kernel K-quant decode), dp4a matvec (- `_blk`block-per-row +- `_sg`subgroup variants), packed-Q8_0 decode with in-kernel fp16 unpack.
- `norm`- `rms_norm`,- `layer_norm`,- `add_rmsnorm`(fused, multi-output).
- `rope`- `rope_half`(GPT-NeoX) and- `rope_interleaved`(GPT-J) conventions.
- `attn`- `sdpa`and- `sdpa_runtime`: GQA + online (flash-style) softmax with a runtime-length KV cache. One stable attention implementation across backends — the structural cure for repetition-collapse.

Run the correctness + throughput gate yourself:

```
```
## Design

Four ideas, borrowed from Rich Hickey and applied to kernels:

- **Decomplect.**Ops, quantization types, and backends are three orthogonal axes braided together in hand-written code. Pulled apart, they compose — you write each axis once.- `backends × types × ops`becomes- `backends + types + ops`.
- **Values, not places.**- [CubeCL](https://github.com/tracel-ai/cubecl)is the lowering engine — the implementation- *value*.- `hanzo_kernel`is the stable- *namespace*you build against; the string- `cubecl`appears in exactly one line of one- `Cargo.toml`. The engine can be upgraded or vendored without touching a kernel.
- **One numeric behavior.**A single source means a single rounding path. The "coherent on Metal, collapsed on CUDA" class of bug cannot occur — not because four copies were tested into agreement, but because there is one copy.
- **Perf-gated migration, never a downgrade.**A hand-tuned kernel is retired for its DSL twin- **only**when the twin is bit-exact- *and*at least as fast. Where a hand-tuned kernel still wins, it stays as the peak path and the DSL is the portable fallback for backends that lack it. Coverage always grows; speed never regresses.

## Status

Published and in production. `rms_norm` and `softmax` are live DSL kernels in the [Hanzo ML](https://github.com/hanzoai/ml) inference engine — their hand-written predecessors are deleted. The full op library is bit-exact on CPU, Vulkan, and Metal, and shelf-ready for the backends still on hand-tuned kernels. A generated DSL kernel dispatches through the engine's real Vulkan and Metal pipelines with `maxerr = 0` — the DSL plugs in as a **code generator**, not a second runtime.

## License

BSD-3-Clause. See [LICENSE](https://docs.rs/LICENSE).

# cu_flight_controller_export - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cu-flight-controller/1.0.0/cu_flight_controller_export/

## Expand description

App-specific Python bindings for offline log inspection.

This module demonstrates the intended Copper pattern for typed Python log access:

- keep the runtime in Rust
- generate the app-specific CopperList type with `gen_cumsgs!`
- expose a tiny `#[pymodule]`wrapper for offline analysis scripts

This is not the same thing as running task logic in Python.

# solana-instructions-sysvar 4.0.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/solana-instructions-sysvar/4.0.0

The serialized instructions of the current transaction.

The *instructions sysvar* provides access to the serialized instruction data
for the currently-running transaction. This allows for [instruction
introspection](https://docs.solanalabs.com/implemented-proposals/instruction_introspection), which is required for correctly interoperating with
native programs like the [secp256k1](https://docs.rs/solana-secp256k1-program/latest/solana_secp256k1_program/) and [ed25519](https://docs.rs/solana-ed25519-program/latest/solana_ed25519_program/) programs.

Unlike other sysvars, the data in the instructions sysvar is not accessed
through a type that implements the [ Sysvar](https://docs.rs/solana-sysvar/latest/solana_sysvar/trait.Sysvar.html) trait. Instead, the
instruction sysvar is accessed through several free functions within this
module.

See also the Solana [documentation on the instructions sysvar](https://docs.solanalabs.com/runtime/sysvars#instructions).

# Examples

For a complete example of how the instructions sysvar is used see the
documentation for [ secp256k1_instruction](https://docs.rs/solana-sdk/latest/solana_sdk/secp256k1_instruction/index.html) in the

`solana-sdk` crate.

---

[73](#73)pub fn construct_instructions_data(

[75](#75)) -> Result<Vec<u8>, InstructionsSysvarError> {
[76](#76)    let mut data = serialize_instructions(instructions)?;

[84](#84)bitflags! {
[85](#85)    struct InstructionsSysvarAccountMeta: u8 {
[86](#86)        const IS_SIGNER = 0b00000001;
[87](#87)        const IS_WRITABLE = 0b00000010;

[91](#91)#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
[92](#92)pub enum InstructionsSysvarError {
[93](#93)    InstructionIndexOutOfBounds,
[95](#95)}
[96](#96)
[97](#97)#[cfg(not(target_os = "solana"))]
[122](#122)#[cfg_attr(feature = "dev-context-only-utils", qualifiers(pub))]
[123](#123)fn serialize_instructions(
[124](#124)    instructions: &[BorrowedInstruction],
[125](#125)) -> Result<Vec<u8>, InstructionsSysvarError> {
[126](#126)    let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(instructions.len() * (32 * 2));
[128](#128)    append_u16(&mut data, instructions.len() as u16);
[129](#129)    for _ in 0..instructions.len() {
[130](#130)        append_u16(&mut data, 0);
[131](#131)    }
[132](#132)
[133](#133)    for (i, instruction) in instructions.iter().enumerate() {
[134](#134)        let start_instruction_offset = u16::try_from(data.len())
[135](#135)            .map_err(|_| InstructionsSysvarError::InstructionIndexOutOfBounds)?;
[136](#136)        let start = 2 + (2 * i);
[137](#137)        data[start..start + 2].copy_from_slice(&start_instruction_offset.to_le_bytes());
[138](#138)        append_u16(&mut data, instruction.accounts.len() as u16);
[139](#139)        for account_meta in &instruction.accounts {
[140](#140)            let mut account_meta_flags = InstructionsSysvarAccountMeta::empty();
[141](#141)            if account_meta.is_signer {
[142](#142)                account_meta_flags |= InstructionsSysvarAccountMeta::IS_SIGNER;
[143](#143)            }
[144](#144)            if account_meta.is_writable {
[145](#145)                account_meta_flags |= InstructionsSysvarAccountMeta::IS_WRITABLE;
[146](#146)            }
[147](#147)            append_u8(&mut data, account_meta_flags.bits());
[148](#148)            append_slice(&mut data, account_meta.pubkey.as_ref());
[149](#149)        }
[150](#150)
[151](#151)        append_slice(&mut data, instruction.program_id.as_ref());
[152](#152)        append_u16(&mut data, instruction.data.len() as u16);
[153](#153)        append_slice(&mut data, instruction.data);
[154](#154)    }
[155](#155)    Ok(data)
[156](#156)}
[157](#157)
[158](#158)fn load_current_index(data: &[u8]) -> u16 {
[166](#166)    let mut instr_fixed_data = [0u8; 2];
[167](#167)    let len = data.len();
[168](#168)    instr_fixed_data.copy_from_slice(&data[len - 2..len]);
[169](#169)    u16::from_le_bytes(instr_fixed_data)
[170](#170)}
[171](#171)
[172](#172)pub fn load_current_index_checked(
[179](#179)    instruction_sysvar_account_info: &AccountInfo,
[180](#180)) -> Result<u16, ProgramError> {
[181](#181)    if !check_id(instruction_sysvar_account_info.key) {
[182](#182)        return Err(ProgramError::UnsupportedSysvar);
[183](#183)    }
[184](#184)
[185](#185)    let instruction_sysvar = instruction_sysvar_account_info.try_borrow_data()?;
[186](#186)    let index = load_current_index(&instruction_sysvar);
[187](#187)    Ok(index)
[188](#188)}
[189](#189)
[190](#190)pub fn store_current_index_checked(
[192](#192)    data: &mut [u8],
[193](#193)    instruction_index: u16,
[194](#194)) -> Result<(), InstructionError> {
[195](#195)    if data.len() < 2 {
[196](#196)        return Err(InstructionError::AccountDataTooSmall);
[197](#197)    }
[198](#198)    let last_index = data.len() - 2;
[199](#199)    data[last_index..last_index + 2].copy_from_slice(&instruction_index.to_le_bytes());
[200](#200)    Ok(())
[201](#201)}
[202](#202)
[203](#203)#[cfg_attr(feature = "dev-context-only-utils", qualifiers(pub))]
[204](#204)fn deserialize_instruction(index: usize, data: &[u8]) -> Result<Instruction, SanitizeError> {
[205](#205)    const IS_SIGNER_BIT: usize = 0;
[206](#206)    const IS_WRITABLE_BIT: usize = 1;
[207](#207)
[208](#208)    let mut current = 0;
[209](#209)    let num_instructions = read_u16(&mut current, data)?;
[210](#210)    if index >= num_instructions as usize {
[211](#211)        return Err(SanitizeError::IndexOutOfBounds);
[212](#212)    }
[213](#213)
[214](#214)    current += index * 2;
[216](#216)    let start = read_u16(&mut current, data)?;
[217](#217)
[218](#218)    current = start as usize;
[219](#219)    let num_accounts = read_u16(&mut current, data)?;
[220](#220)    let mut accounts = Vec::with_capacity(num_accounts as usize);
[221](#221)    for _ in 0..num_accounts {
[222](#222)        let meta_byte = read_u8(&mut current, data)?;
[223](#223)        let mut is_signer = false;
[224](#224)        let mut is_writable = false;
[225](#225)        if meta_byte & (1 << IS_SIGNER_BIT) != 0 {
[226](#226)            is_signer = true;
[227](#227)        }
[228](#228)        if meta_byte & (1 << IS_WRITABLE_BIT) != 0 {
[229](#229)            is_writable = true;
[230](#230)        }
[231](#231)        let pubkey = read_pubkey(&mut current, data)?;
[232](#232)        accounts.push(AccountMeta {
[233](#233)            pubkey,
[234](#234)            is_signer,
[235](#235)            is_writable,
[236](#236)        });
[237](#237)    }
[238](#238)    let program_id = read_pubkey(&mut current, data)?;
[239](#239)    let data_len = read_u16(&mut current, data)?;
[240](#240)    let data = read_slice(&mut current, data, data_len as usize)?;
[241](#241)    Ok(Instruction {
[242](#242)        program_id,
[243](#243)        accounts,
[244](#244)        data,
[245](#245)    })
[246](#246)}

[256](#256)fn load_instruction_at(index: usize, data: &[u8]) -> Result<Instruction, SanitizeError> {
[257](#257)    deserialize_instruction(index, data)
[258](#258)}
[259](#259)
[260](#260)pub fn load_instruction_at_checked(
[267](#267)    index: usize,
[268](#268)    instruction_sysvar_account_info: &AccountInfo,
[269](#269)) -> Result<Instruction, ProgramError> {
[270](#270)    if !check_id(instruction_sysvar_account_info.key) {
[271](#271)        return Err(ProgramError::UnsupportedSysvar);
[272](#272)    }
[273](#273)
[274](#274)    let instruction_sysvar = instruction_sysvar_account_info.try_borrow_data()?;
[275](#275)    load_instruction_at(index, &instruction_sysvar).map_err(|err| match err {
[276](#276)        SanitizeError::IndexOutOfBounds => ProgramError::InvalidArgument,
[277](#277)        _ => ProgramError::InvalidInstructionData,
[278](#278)    })
[279](#279)}
[280](#280)
[281](#281)pub fn get_instruction_relative(
[288](#288)    index_relative_to_current: i64,
[289](#289)    instruction_sysvar_account_info: &AccountInfo,
[290](#290)) -> Result<Instruction, ProgramError> {
[291](#291)    if !check_id(instruction_sysvar_account_info.key) {
[292](#292)        return Err(ProgramError::UnsupportedSysvar);
[293](#293)    }
[294](#294)
[295](#295)    let instruction_sysvar = instruction_sysvar_account_info.data.borrow();
[296](#296)    let current_index = load_current_index(&instruction_sysvar) as i64;
[297](#297)    let index = current_index.saturating_add(index_relative_to_current);
[298](#298)    if index < 0 {
[299](#299)        return Err(ProgramError::InvalidArgument);
[300](#300)    }
[301](#301)    load_instruction_at(
[302](#302)        current_index.saturating_add(index_relative_to_current) as usize,
[303](#303)        &instruction_sysvar,
[304](#304)    )
[305](#305)    .map_err(|err| match err {
[306](#306)        SanitizeError::IndexOutOfBounds => ProgramError::InvalidArgument,
[307](#307)        _ => ProgramError::InvalidInstructionData,
[308](#308)    })
[309](#309)}

[349](#349)    fn make_borrowed_instruction(params: &MakeInstructionParams) -> BorrowedInstruction<'_> {
[350](#350)        let MakeInstructionParams {
[351](#351)            program_id,
[352](#352)            account_key,
[353](#353)            is_signer,
[354](#354)            is_writable,
[355](#355)        } = params;
[356](#356)        BorrowedInstruction {
[357](#357)            program_id,
[358](#358)            accounts: vec![BorrowedAccountMeta {
[359](#359)                pubkey: account_key,
[360](#360)                is_signer: *is_signer,
[361](#361)                is_writable: *is_writable,

[364](#364)        }
[365](#365)    }

[385](#385)    #[test]
[386](#386)    fn test_load_instruction_at_checked() {
[387](#387)        let program_id0 = Address::new_unique();
[388](#388)        let program_id1 = Address::new_unique();
[389](#389)        let account_key0 = Address::new_unique();
[390](#390)        let account_key1 = Address::new_unique();
[391](#391)        let params0 = MakeInstructionParams {
[392](#392)            program_id: program_id0,
[393](#393)            account_key: account_key0,
[394](#394)            is_signer: false,
[395](#395)            is_writable: false,
[396](#396)        };
[397](#397)        let params1 = MakeInstructionParams {
[398](#398)            program_id: program_id1,
[399](#399)            account_key: account_key1,
[400](#400)            is_signer: false,
[401](#401)            is_writable: false,
[402](#402)        };
[403](#403)        let instruction0 = make_instruction(params0);
[404](#404)        let instruction1 = make_instruction(params1);
[405](#405)        let borrowed_instruction0 = make_borrowed_instruction(¶ms0);
[406](#406)        let borrowed_instruction1 = make_borrowed_instruction(¶ms1);
[407](#407)        let key = id();
[408](#408)        let mut lamports = 0;
[409](#409)        let mut data =
[410](#410)            construct_instructions_data(&[borrowed_instruction0, borrowed_instruction1]).unwrap();
[411](#411)        let owner = solana_sdk_ids::sysvar::id();
[412](#412)        let mut account_info =
[413](#413)            AccountInfo::new(&key, false, false, &mut lamports, &mut data, &owner, false);
[414](#414)
[415](#415)        assert_eq!(
[416](#416)            instruction0,
[417](#417)            load_instruction_at_checked(0, &account_info).unwrap()
[418](#418)        );
[419](#419)        assert_eq!(
[420](#420)            instruction1,
[421](#421)            load_instruction_at_checked(1, &account_info).unwrap()
[422](#422)        );
[423](#423)        assert_eq!(
[424](#424)            Err(ProgramError::InvalidArgument),
[425](#425)            load_instruction_at_checked(2, &account_info)
[426](#426)        );
[427](#427)
[428](#428)        let key = Address::new_unique();
[429](#429)        account_info.key = &key;
[430](#430)        assert_eq!(
[431](#431)            Err(ProgramError::UnsupportedSysvar),
[432](#432)            load_instruction_at_checked(2, &account_info)
[433](#433)        );
[434](#434)    }

[437](#437)    fn test_load_current_index_checked() {
[438](#438)        let program_id0 = Address::new_unique();
[439](#439)        let program_id1 = Address::new_unique();
[440](#440)        let account_key0 = Address::new_unique();
[441](#441)        let account_key1 = Address::new_unique();
[442](#442)        let params0 = MakeInstructionParams {
[443](#443)            program_id: program_id0,
[444](#444)            account_key: account_key0,
[445](#445)            is_signer: false,
[446](#446)            is_writable: false,
[447](#447)        };
[448](#448)        let params1 = MakeInstructionParams {
[449](#449)            program_id: program_id1,
[450](#450)            account_key: account_key1,
[451](#451)            is_signer: false,
[452](#452)            is_writable: false,
[453](#453)        };
[454](#454)        let borrowed_instruction0 = make_borrowed_instruction(¶ms0);
[455](#455)        let borrowed_instruction1 = make_borrowed_instruction(¶ms1);
[456](#456)
[457](#457)        let key = id();
[458](#458)        let mut lamports = 0;
[459](#459)        let mut data =
[460](#460)            construct_instructions_data(&[borrowed_instruction0, borrowed_instruction1]).unwrap();
[461](#461)        let res = store_current_index_checked(&mut data, 1);
[462](#462)        assert!(res.is_ok());
[463](#463)        let owner = solana_sdk_ids::sysvar::id();
[464](#464)        let mut account_info =
[465](#465)            AccountInfo::new(&key, false, false, &mut lamports, &mut data, &owner, false);
[466](#466)
[467](#467)        assert_eq!(1, load_current_index_checked(&account_info).unwrap());
[468](#468)        {
[469](#469)            let mut data = account_info.try_borrow_mut_data().unwrap();
[470](#470)            let res = store_current_index_checked(&mut data, 0);
[471](#471)            assert!(res.is_ok());
[472](#472)        }
[473](#473)        assert_eq!(0, load_current_index_checked(&account_info).unwrap());
[474](#474)
[475](#475)        let key = Address::new_unique();
[476](#476)        account_info.key = &key;
[477](#477)        assert_eq!(
[478](#478)            Err(ProgramError::UnsupportedSysvar),
[479](#479)            load_current_index_checked(&account_info)
[480](#480)        );
[481](#481)    }

[484](#484)    fn test_get_instruction_relative() {
[485](#485)        let program_id0 = Address::new_unique();
[486](#486)        let program_id1 = Address::new_unique();
[487](#487)        let program_id2 = Address::new_unique();
[488](#488)        let account_key0 = Address::new_unique();
[489](#489)        let account_key1 = Address::new_unique();
[490](#490)        let account_key2 = Address::new_unique();
[491](#491)        let params0 = MakeInstructionParams {
[492](#492)            program_id: program_id0,
[493](#493)            account_key: account_key0,
[494](#494)            is_signer: false,
[495](#495)            is_writable: false,
[496](#496)        };
[497](#497)        let params1 = MakeInstructionParams {
[498](#498)            program_id: program_id1,
[499](#499)            account_key: account_key1,
[500](#500)            is_signer: false,
[501](#501)            is_writable: false,
[502](#502)        };
[503](#503)        let params2 = MakeInstructionParams {
[504](#504)            program_id: program_id2,
[505](#505)            account_key: account_key2,
[506](#506)            is_signer: false,
[507](#507)            is_writable: false,
[508](#508)        };
[509](#509)        let instruction0 = make_instruction(params0);
[510](#510)        let instruction1 = make_instruction(params1);
[511](#511)        let instruction2 = make_instruction(params2);
[512](#512)        let borrowed_instruction0 = make_borrowed_instruction(¶ms0);
[513](#513)        let borrowed_instruction1 = make_borrowed_instruction(¶ms1);
[514](#514)        let borrowed_instruction2 = make_borrowed_instruction(¶ms2);
[515](#515)
[516](#516)        let key = id();
[517](#517)        let mut lamports = 0;
[518](#518)        let mut data = construct_instructions_data(&[
[519](#519)            borrowed_instruction0,

[521](#521)            borrowed_instruction2,
[522](#522)        ])
[523](#523)        .unwrap();
[524](#524)        let res = store_current_index_checked(&mut data, 1);
[525](#525)        assert!(res.is_ok());
[526](#526)        let owner = solana_sdk_ids::sysvar::id();
[527](#527)        let mut account_info =
[528](#528)            AccountInfo::new(&key, false, false, &mut lamports, &mut data, &owner, false);
[529](#529)
[530](#530)        assert_eq!(
[531](#531)            Err(ProgramError::InvalidArgument),
[532](#532)            get_instruction_relative(-2, &account_info)
[533](#533)        );
[534](#534)        assert_eq!(
[535](#535)            instruction0,
[536](#536)            get_instruction_relative(-1, &account_info).unwrap()
[537](#537)        );
[538](#538)        assert_eq!(
[539](#539)            instruction1,
[540](#540)            get_instruction_relative(0, &account_info).unwrap()
[541](#541)        );
[542](#542)        assert_eq!(
[543](#543)            instruction2,
[544](#544)            get_instruction_relative(1, &account_info).unwrap()
[545](#545)        );
[546](#546)        assert_eq!(
[547](#547)            Err(ProgramError::InvalidArgument),
[548](#548)            get_instruction_relative(2, &account_info)
[549](#549)        );
[550](#550)        {
[551](#551)            let mut data = account_info.try_borrow_mut_data().unwrap();
[552](#552)            let res = store_current_index_checked(&mut data, 0);
[553](#553)            assert!(res.is_ok());
[554](#554)        }
[555](#555)        assert_eq!(
[556](#556)            Err(ProgramError::InvalidArgument),

[558](#558)        );

[562](#562)        );

# solana_instructions_sysvar - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/solana-instructions-sysvar/latest/solana_instructions_sysvar/

## Expand description

The serialized instructions of the current transaction.

The *instructions sysvar* provides access to the serialized instruction data
for the currently-running transaction. This allows for [instruction
introspection](https://docs.solanalabs.com/implemented-proposals/instruction_introspection), which is required for correctly interoperating with
native programs like the [secp256k1](https://docs.rs/solana-secp256k1-program/latest/solana_secp256k1_program/) and [ed25519](https://docs.rs/solana-ed25519-program/latest/solana_ed25519_program/) programs.

Unlike other sysvars, the data in the instructions sysvar is not accessed
through a type that implements the [ Sysvar](https://docs.rs/solana-sysvar/latest/solana_sysvar/trait.Sysvar.html) trait. Instead, the
instruction sysvar is accessed through several free functions within this
module.

See also the Solana [documentation on the instructions sysvar](https://docs.solanalabs.com/runtime/sysvars#instructions).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

For a complete example of how the instructions sysvar is used see the
documentation for [ secp256k1_instruction](https://docs.rs/solana-sdk/latest/solana_sdk/secp256k1_instruction/index.html) in the

`solana-sdk` crate.## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Instructions](https://docs.rs/struct.Instructions.html)
- Instructions sysvar, dummy type.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [ID](https://docs.rs/constant.ID.html)
- The const program ID.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [check_](https://docs.rs/fn.check_id.html)- id
- Returns `true`if given address is the ID.
- [construct_](https://docs.rs/fn.construct_instructions_data.html)- instructions_ - data - Non- - `target_os=solana`
- Construct the account data for the instructions sysvar.
- [deserialize_](https://docs.rs/fn.deserialize_instruction.html)- instruction
- [get_](https://docs.rs/fn.get_instruction_relative.html)- instruction_ - relative
- Returns the `Instruction`relative to the current`Instruction`in the currently executing`Transaction`.
- [id](https://docs.rs/fn.id.html)
- Returns the ID.
- [load_](https://docs.rs/fn.load_current_index_checked.html)- current_ - index_ - checked
- Load the current `Instruction`’s index in the currently executing`Transaction`.
- [load_](https://docs.rs/fn.load_instruction_at.html)- instruction_ - at
- Load an `Instruction`in the currently executing`Transaction`at the specified index.
- [load_](https://docs.rs/fn.load_instruction_at_checked.html)- instruction_ - at_ - checked
- Load an `Instruction`in the currently executing`Transaction`at the specified index.
- [serialize_](https://docs.rs/fn.serialize_instructions.html)- instructions
- [store_](https://docs.rs/fn.store_current_index_checked.html)- current_ - index_ - checked
- Store the current `Instruction`’s index in the instructions sysvar data.

# solana-instructions-sysvar 4.0.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/solana-instructions-sysvar/latest/builds

All the builds on docs.rs are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The limits for this crate are the following:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                    If a build fails because it hit one of those limits please
                    [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                    to get them increased.

# qualifier_attr 0.2.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/qualifier_attr/^0.2.2

# qualifier_attr

Procedural macro attributes for adding "qualifiers" to various items.

At the moment, the crate supports the following "qualifiers":

- `pub`,- `pub(crate)`, etc. - visibility and restriction
- `default`- default implementations (a feature of- [specialization](https://doc.rust-lang.org/unstable-book/language-features/specialization.html))
- `async`- asynchronous code, e.g.- `async fn`
- `unsafe`- unsafe code, e.g.- `unsafe fn`,- `unsafe trait`
- `const`- code that may run at compile time, e.g.- `const fn`
- `extern "ABI"`- specifying an ABI, e.g.- `extern "C" fn`

## Limitations

- It seems that rust-analyzer will sometimes complain when the attribute is used with modules.

## Examples

```
extern crate qualifier_attr;
// We can add a qualifier to a function
// with an attribute.
const CONST_RES: u32 = const_fn;
// It's not so impressive on its own,
// but with `cfg_attr`, it can be conditional.
// It even works with types, imports, and more!
use Foo;
// Traits and implementations too!?
// You can add qualifiers to the fields of a
// struct as well with this special attribute.
;
```
Learn more about `cfg_attr` [here](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/conditional-compilation.html#the-cfg_attr-attribute).

## Note on legacy attributes

Before version 0.2.0, this crate provided a separate attribute for each kind of item. While this should generally be a small win for compile times, it is generally not justified by the additional complexity. The legacy attributes are still available behind the default `legacy_attrs` feature flag, but their use is currently discouraged. In order to disable the legacy attributes, add the following to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = {  = "0.2",  = false }
```

# solana-instruction 3.4.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/solana-instruction/^3.4.0

Types for directing the execution of Solana programs.

Every invocation of a Solana program executes a single instruction, as
defined by the [`Instruction`] type. An instruction is primarily a vector of
bytes, the contents of which are program-specific, and not interpreted by
the Solana runtime. This allows flexibility in how programs behave, how they
are controlled by client software, and what data encodings they use.

Besides the instruction data, every account a program may read or write
while executing a given instruction is also included in `Instruction`, as
[`AccountMeta`] values. The runtime uses this information to efficiently
schedule execution of transactions.

---

# solana-sysvar-id 3.1.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/solana-sysvar-id/^3.0.0

Access to special accounts with dynamically-updated data.

Sysvars are special accounts that contain dynamically-updated data about the
network cluster, the blockchain history, and the executing transaction. Each
sysvar is defined in its own crate. The [ clock](https://docs.rs/solana-clock/latest),

[,](https://docs.rs/solana-epoch-schedule/latest)

`epoch_schedule`[, and](https://docs.rs/solana-program/latest/solana_program/sysvar/instructions)

`instructions`[sysvars are most useful to on-chain programs.](https://docs.rs/solana-rent/latest)

`rent`All sysvar accounts are owned by the account identified by [ solana_sysvar::ID](crate::ID).

For more details see the Solana [documentation on sysvars](https://docs.solanalabs.com/runtime/sysvars).

---

# solana-address 2.6.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/solana-address/^2.6.1

Address representation for Solana.

An address is a sequence of 32 bytes, often shown as a base58 encoded string (e.g. 14grJpemFaf88c8tiVb77W7TYg2W3ir6pfkKz3YjhhZ5).

Address representation for Solana.

An address is a sequence of 32 bytes, often shown as a base58 encoded string (e.g. 14grJpemFaf88c8tiVb77W7TYg2W3ir6pfkKz3YjhhZ5).

# bitflags 2.13.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bitflags/^2.8.0

# bitflags

`bitflags` generates flags enums with well-defined semantics and ergonomic end-user APIs.

You can use `bitflags` to:

- provide more user-friendly bindings to C APIs where flags may or may not be fully known in advance.
- generate efficient options types with string parsing and formatting support.

You can't use `bitflags` to:

-
guarantee only bits corresponding to defined flags will ever be set. `bitflags`allows access to the underlying bits type so arbitrary bits may be set.
-
define bitfields. `bitflags`only generates types where set bits denote the presence of some combination of flags.

## Usage

Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "2.13.0"
```
and this to your source code:

```
use bitflags;
```
## Example

Generate a flags structure:

```
use bitflags;
// The `bitflags!` macro generates `struct`s that manage a set of flags.
bitflags!
```
## Cargo features

The `bitflags` library defines a few Cargo features that you can opt-in to:

- `std`: Implement the- `Error`trait on error types used by- `bitflags`.
- `serde`: Support deriving- `serde`traits on generated flags types.
- `arbitrary`: Support deriving- `arbitrary`traits on generated flags types.
- `bytemuck`: Support deriving- `bytemuck`traits on generated flags types.

Also see [ bitflags_derive](https://github.com/bitflags/bitflags-derive) for other flags-aware traits.

## Rust Version Support

The minimum supported Rust version is documented in the `Cargo.toml` file.
This may be bumped in minor releases as necessary.

---

# solana-instructions-sysvar 3.0.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/solana-instructions-sysvar/3.0.1

The serialized instructions of the current transaction.

The *instructions sysvar* provides access to the serialized instruction data
for the currently-running transaction. This allows for [instruction
introspection](https://docs.solanalabs.com/implemented-proposals/instruction_introspection), which is required for correctly interoperating with
native programs like the [secp256k1](https://docs.rs/solana-secp256k1-program/latest/solana_secp256k1_program/) and [ed25519](https://docs.rs/solana-ed25519-program/latest/solana_ed25519_program/) programs.

Unlike other sysvars, the data in the instructions sysvar is not accessed
through a type that implements the [ Sysvar](https://docs.rs/solana-sysvar/latest/solana_sysvar/trait.Sysvar.html) trait. Instead, the
instruction sysvar is accessed through several free functions within this
module.

See also the Solana [documentation on the instructions sysvar](https://docs.solanalabs.com/runtime/sysvars#instructions).

# Examples

For a complete example of how the instructions sysvar is used see the
documentation for [ secp256k1_instruction](https://docs.rs/solana-sdk/latest/solana_sdk/secp256k1_instruction/index.html) in the

`solana-sdk` crate.

---

# qualifier_attr 0.2.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/qualifier_attr/0.2.2

# qualifier_attr

Procedural macro attributes for adding "qualifiers" to various items.

At the moment, the crate supports the following "qualifiers":

- `pub`,- `pub(crate)`, etc. - visibility and restriction
- `default`- default implementations (a feature of- [specialization](https://doc.rust-lang.org/unstable-book/language-features/specialization.html))
- `async`- asynchronous code, e.g.- `async fn`
- `unsafe`- unsafe code, e.g.- `unsafe fn`,- `unsafe trait`
- `const`- code that may run at compile time, e.g.- `const fn`
- `extern "ABI"`- specifying an ABI, e.g.- `extern "C" fn`

## Limitations

- It seems that rust-analyzer will sometimes complain when the attribute is used with modules.

## Examples

```
extern crate qualifier_attr;
// We can add a qualifier to a function
// with an attribute.
const CONST_RES: u32 = const_fn;
// It's not so impressive on its own,
// but with `cfg_attr`, it can be conditional.
// It even works with types, imports, and more!
use Foo;
// Traits and implementations too!?
// You can add qualifiers to the fields of a
// struct as well with this special attribute.
;
```
Learn more about `cfg_attr` [here](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/conditional-compilation.html#the-cfg_attr-attribute).

## Note on legacy attributes

Before version 0.2.0, this crate provided a separate attribute for each kind of item. While this should generally be a small win for compile times, it is generally not justified by the additional complexity. The legacy attributes are still available behind the default `legacy_attrs` feature flag, but their use is currently discouraged. In order to disable the legacy attributes, add the following to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = {  = "0.2",  = false }
```

---

# proc_macro2 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/^1/

## Expand description

A wrapper around the procedural macro API of the compiler’s [ proc_macro](https://doc.rust-lang.org/proc_macro/index.html)
crate. This library serves two purposes:

-
**Bring proc-macro-like functionality to other contexts like build.rs and main.rs.**Types from`proc_macro`are entirely specific to procedural macros and cannot ever exist in code outside of a procedural macro. Meanwhile`proc_macro2`types may exist anywhere including non-macro code. By developing foundational libraries like[syn](https://github.com/dtolnay/syn)and[quote](https://github.com/dtolnay/quote)against`proc_macro2`rather than`proc_macro`, the procedural macro ecosystem becomes easily applicable to many other use cases and we avoid reimplementing non-macro equivalents of those libraries.
-
**Make procedural macros unit testable.**As a consequence of being specific to procedural macros, nothing that uses`proc_macro`can be executed from a unit test. In order for helper libraries or components of a macro to be testable in isolation, they must be implemented using`proc_macro2`.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

The skeleton of a typical procedural macro typically looks like this:

```
extern crate proc_macro;
#[proc_macro_derive(MyDerive)]
pub fn my_derive(input: proc_macro::TokenStream) -> proc_macro::TokenStream {
    let input = proc_macro2::TokenStream::from(input);
    let output: proc_macro2::TokenStream = {
        /* transform input */
    };
    proc_macro::TokenStream::from(output)
}
```
If parsing with [Syn](https://github.com/dtolnay/syn), you’ll use [ parse_macro_input!](https://docs.rs/syn/2.0/syn/macro.parse_macro_input.html) instead to
propagate parse errors correctly back to the compiler when parsing fails.

[§](https://docs.rs#unstable-features)Unstable features

The default feature set of proc-macro2 tracks the most recent stable
compiler API. Functionality in `proc_macro` that is not yet stable is not
exposed by proc-macro2 by default.

To opt into the additional APIs available in the most recent nightly
compiler, the `procmacro2_semver_exempt` config flag must be passed to
rustc. We will polyfill those nightly-only APIs back to Rust 1.68.0. As
these are unstable APIs that track the nightly compiler, minor versions of
proc-macro2 may make breaking changes to them at any time.

`RUSTFLAGS='--cfg procmacro2_semver_exempt' cargo build`Note that this must not only be done for your crate, but for any crate that depends on your crate. This infectious nature is intentional, as it serves as a reminder that you are outside of the normal semver guarantees.

Semver exempt methods are marked as such in the proc-macro2 documentation.

[§](https://docs.rs#thread-safety)Thread-Safety

Most types in this crate are `!Sync` because the underlying compiler
types make use of thread-local memory, meaning they cannot be accessed from
a different thread.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [extra](https://docs.rs/extra/index.html)
- Items which do not have a correspondence to any API in the proc_macro crate, but are necessary to include in proc-macro2.
- [token_](https://docs.rs/token_stream/index.html)- stream
- Public implementation details for the `TokenStream`type, such as iterators.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Group](https://docs.rs/struct.Group.html)
- A delimited token stream.
- [Ident](https://docs.rs/struct.Ident.html)
- A word of Rust code, which may be a keyword or legal variable name.
- [LexError](https://docs.rs/struct.LexError.html)
- Error returned from `TokenStream::from_str`.
- [Line](https://docs.rs/struct.LineColumn.html)- Column - `span-locations`
- A line-column pair representing the start or end of a `Span`.
- [Literal](https://docs.rs/struct.Literal.html)
- A literal string (`"hello"`), byte string (`b"hello"`), character (`'a'`), byte character (`b'a'`), an integer or floating point number with or without a suffix (`1`,`1u8`,`2.3`,`2.3f32`).
- [Punct](https://docs.rs/struct.Punct.html)
- A `Punct`is a single punctuation character like`+`,`-`or`#`.
- [Span](https://docs.rs/struct.Span.html)
- A region of source code, along with macro expansion information.
- [Token](https://docs.rs/struct.TokenStream.html)- Stream
- An abstract stream of tokens, or more concretely a sequence of token trees.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Conversion](https://docs.rs/enum.ConversionErrorKind.html)- Error - Kind - `procmacro2_semver_exempt`
- Error when retrieving a string literal’s unescaped value.
- [Delimiter](https://docs.rs/enum.Delimiter.html)
- Describes how a sequence of token trees is delimited.
- [Escape](https://docs.rs/enum.EscapeError.html)- Error - `procmacro2_semver_exempt`
- Errors and warnings that can occur during string, char, and byte unescaping.
- [Spacing](https://docs.rs/enum.Spacing.html)
- Whether a `Punct`is followed immediately by another`Punct`or followed by another token or whitespace.
- [Token](https://docs.rs/enum.TokenTree.html)- Tree
- A single token or a delimited sequence of token trees (e.g. `[1, (), ..]`).

---

# quote - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/quote/^1/

## Expand description

This crate provides the [ quote!](https://docs.rs/macro.quote.html) macro for turning Rust syntax tree data
structures into tokens of source code.

Procedural macros in Rust receive a stream of tokens as input, execute arbitrary Rust code to determine how to manipulate those tokens, and produce a stream of tokens to hand back to the compiler to compile into the caller’s crate. Quasi-quoting is a solution to one piece of that — producing tokens to return to the compiler.

The idea of quasi-quoting is that we write *code* that we treat as *data*.
Within the `quote!` macro, we can write what looks like code to our text
editor or IDE. We get all the benefits of the editor’s brace matching,
syntax highlighting, indentation, and maybe autocompletion. But rather than
compiling that as code into the current crate, we can treat it as data, pass
it around, mutate it, and eventually hand it back to the compiler as tokens
to compile into the macro caller’s crate.

This crate is motivated by the procedural macro use case, but is a general-purpose Rust quasi-quoting library and is not specific to procedural macros.

```
[dependencies]
quote = "1.0"
```
[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

The following quasi-quoted block of code is something you might find in [a](https://serde.rs/)
procedural macro having to do with data structure serialization. The `#var`
syntax performs interpolation of runtime variables into the quoted tokens.
Check out the documentation of the [ quote!](https://docs.rs/macro.quote.html) macro for more detail about
the syntax. See also the

[macro which is important for implementing hygienic procedural macros.](https://docs.rs/macro.quote_spanned.html)

`quote_spanned!````
let tokens = quote! {
    struct SerializeWith #generics #where_clause {
        value: &'a #field_ty,
        phantom: core::marker::PhantomData<#item_ty>,
    }
    impl #generics serde::Serialize for SerializeWith #generics #where_clause {
        fn serialize<S>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error>
        where
            S: serde::Serializer,
        {
            #path(self.value, serializer)
        }
    }
    SerializeWith {
        value: #value,
        phantom: core::marker::PhantomData::<#item_ty>,
    }
};
```
[§](https://docs.rs#non-macro-code-generators)Non-macro code generators

When using `quote` in a build.rs or main.rs and writing the output out to a
file, consider having the code generator pass the tokens through
[prettyplease](https://github.com/dtolnay/prettyplease) before writing. This way if an error occurs in the generated
code it is convenient for a human to read and debug.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [format_](https://docs.rs/macro.format_ident.html)- ident
- Formatting macro for constructing `Ident`s.
- [quote](https://docs.rs/macro.quote.html)
- The whole point.
- [quote_](https://docs.rs/macro.quote_spanned.html)- spanned
- Same as `quote!`, but applies a given span to all tokens originating within the macro invocation.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Ident](https://docs.rs/trait.IdentFragment.html)- Fragment
- Specialized formatting trait used by `format_ident!`.
- [ToTokens](https://docs.rs/trait.ToTokens.html)
- Types that can be interpolated inside a `quote!`invocation.
- [Token](https://docs.rs/trait.TokenStreamExt.html)- Stream - Ext
- TokenStream extension trait with methods for appending tokens.

---

# syn - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/syn/^2/

## Expand description

Syn is a parsing library for parsing a stream of Rust tokens into a syntax tree of Rust source code.

Currently this library is geared toward use in Rust procedural macros, but contains some APIs that may be useful more generally.

-
**Data structures**— Syn provides a complete syntax tree that can represent any valid Rust source code. The syntax tree is rooted at`syn::File``syn::Item``syn::Expr``syn::Type`
-
**Derives**— Of particular interest to derive macros is`syn::DeriveInput`
-
**Parsing**— Parsing in Syn is built around[parser functions](https://docs.rs/parse/index.html)with the signature`fn(ParseStream) -> Result<T>`. Every syntax tree node defined by Syn is individually parsable and may be used as a building block for custom syntaxes, or you may dream up your own brand new syntax without involving any of our syntax tree types.
-
**Location information**— Every token parsed by Syn is associated with a`Span`that tracks line and column information back to the source of that token. These spans allow a procedural macro to display detailed error messages pointing to all the right places in the user’s code. There is an example of this below.
-
**Feature flags**— Functionality is aggressively feature gated so your procedural macros enable only what they need, and do not pay in compile time for all the rest.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-of-a-derive-macro)Example of a derive macro

The canonical derive macro using Syn looks like this. We write an ordinary
Rust function tagged with a `proc_macro_derive` attribute and the name of
the trait we are deriving. Any time that derive appears in the user’s code,
the Rust compiler passes their data structure as tokens into our macro. We
get to execute arbitrary Rust code to figure out what to do with those
tokens, then hand some tokens back to the compiler to compile into the
user’s crate.

```
[dependencies]
syn = "2.0"
quote = "1.0"
[lib]
proc-macro = true
```
```
use proc_macro::TokenStream;
use quote::quote;
use syn::{parse_macro_input, DeriveInput};
#[proc_macro_derive(MyMacro)]
pub fn my_macro(input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
    // Parse the input tokens into a syntax tree
    let input = parse_macro_input!(input as DeriveInput);
    // Build the output, possibly using quasi-quotation
    let expanded = quote! {
        // ...
    };
    // Hand the output tokens back to the compiler
    TokenStream::from(expanded)
}
```
The [ heapsize](https://github.com/dtolnay/syn/tree/master/examples/heapsize) example directory shows a complete working implementation
of a derive macro. The example derives a

`HeapSize` trait which computes an
estimate of the amount of heap memory owned by a value.```
pub trait HeapSize {
    /// Total number of bytes of heap memory owned by `self`.
    fn heap_size_of_children(&self) -> usize;
}
```
The derive macro allows users to write `#[derive(HeapSize)]` on data
structures in their program.

```
#[derive(HeapSize)]
struct Demo<'a, T: ?Sized> {
    a: Box<T>,
    b: u8,
    c: &'a str,
    d: String,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#spans-and-error-reporting)Spans and error reporting

The token-based procedural macro API provides great control over where the
compiler’s error messages are displayed in user code. Consider the error the
user sees if one of their field types does not implement `HeapSize`.

```
#[derive(HeapSize)]
struct Broken {
    ok: String,
    bad: std::thread::Thread,
}
```
By tracking span information all the way through the expansion of a
procedural macro as shown in the `heapsize` example, token-based macros in
Syn are able to trigger errors that directly pinpoint the source of the
problem.

```
error[E0277]: the trait bound `std::thread::Thread: HeapSize` is not satisfied
 --> src/main.rs:7:5
  |
7 |     bad: std::thread::Thread,
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ the trait `HeapSize` is not implemented for `Thread`
```
[§](https://docs.rs#parsing-a-custom-syntax)Parsing a custom syntax

The [ lazy-static](https://github.com/dtolnay/syn/tree/master/examples/lazy-static) example directory shows the implementation of a

`functionlike!(...)` procedural macro in which the input tokens are parsed
using Syn’s parsing API.The example reimplements the popular `lazy_static` crate from crates.io as a
procedural macro.

```
lazy_static! {
    static ref USERNAME: Regex = Regex::new("^[a-z0-9_-]{3,16}$").unwrap();
}
```
The implementation shows how to trigger custom warnings and error messages on the macro input.

```
warning: come on, pick a more creative name
  --> src/main.rs:10:16
   |
10 |     static ref FOO: String = "lazy_static".to_owned();
   |                ^^^
```
[§](https://docs.rs#testing)Testing

When testing macros, we often care not just that the macro can be used
successfully but also that when the macro is provided with invalid input it
produces maximally helpful error messages. Consider using the [ trybuild](https://github.com/dtolnay/trybuild)
crate to write tests for errors that are emitted by your macro or errors
detected by the Rust compiler in the expanded code following misuse of the
macro. Such tests help avoid regressions from later refactors that
mistakenly make an error no longer trigger or be less helpful than it used
to be.

[§](https://docs.rs#debugging)Debugging

When developing a procedural macro it can be helpful to look at what the
generated code looks like. Use `cargo rustc -- -Zunstable-options -Zunpretty=expanded` or the [ cargo expand](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-expand) subcommand.

To show the expanded code for some crate that uses your procedural macro,
run `cargo expand` from that crate. To show the expanded code for one of
your own test cases, run `cargo expand --test the_test_case` where the last
argument is the name of the test file without the `.rs` extension.

This write-up by Brandon W Maister discusses debugging in more detail:
[Debugging Rust’s new Custom Derive system](https://quodlibetor.github.io/posts/debugging-rusts-new-custom-derive-system/).

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-features)Optional features

Syn puts a lot of functionality behind optional features in order to optimize compile time for the most common use cases. The following features are available.

- `derive`- *(enabled by default)*— Data structures for representing the possible input to a derive macro, including structs and enums and types.
- `full`
- `parsing`- *(enabled by default)*— Ability to parse input tokens into a syntax tree node of a chosen type.
- `printing`- *(enabled by default)*— Ability to print a syntax tree node as tokens of Rust source code.
- `visit`
- `visit-mut`
- `fold`
- `clone-impls`- *(enabled by default)*— Clone impls for all syntax tree types.
- `extra-traits`
- `proc-macro`- *(enabled by default)*— Runtime dependency on the dynamic library libproc_macro from rustc toolchain.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [buffer](https://docs.rs/buffer/index.html)- `parsing`
- A stably addressed token buffer supporting efficient traversal based on a cheaply copyable cursor.
- [ext](https://docs.rs/ext/index.html)
- Extension traits to provide parsing methods on foreign types.
- [fold](https://docs.rs/fold/index.html)- `fold`
- Syntax tree traversal to transform the nodes of an owned syntax tree.
- [meta](https://docs.rs/meta/index.html)- `parsing`and (- `derive`or- `full`)
- Facility for interpreting structured content inside of an `Attribute`.
- [parse](https://docs.rs/parse/index.html)- `parsing`
- Parsing interface for parsing a token stream into a syntax tree node.
- [punctuated](https://docs.rs/punctuated/index.html)
- A punctuated sequence of syntax tree nodes separated by punctuation.
- [spanned](https://docs.rs/spanned/index.html)- `parsing`and- `printing`
- A trait that can provide the `Span`of the complete contents of a syntax tree node.
- [token](https://docs.rs/token/index.html)
- Tokens representing Rust punctuation, keywords, and delimiters.
- [visit](https://docs.rs/visit/index.html)- `visit`
- Syntax tree traversal to walk a shared borrow of a syntax tree.
- [visit_](https://docs.rs/visit_mut/index.html)- mut - `visit-mut`
- Syntax tree traversal to mutate an exclusive borrow of a syntax tree in place.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [Token](https://docs.rs/macro.Token.html)
- A type-macro that expands to the name of the Rust type representation of a given token.
- [braced](https://docs.rs/macro.braced.html)- `parsing`
- Parse a set of curly braces and expose their content to subsequent parsers.
- [bracketed](https://docs.rs/macro.bracketed.html)- `parsing`
- Parse a set of square brackets and expose their content to subsequent parsers.
- [custom_](https://docs.rs/macro.custom_keyword.html)- keyword
- Define a type that supports parsing and printing a given identifier as if it were a keyword.
- [custom_](https://docs.rs/macro.custom_punctuation.html)- punctuation
- Define a type that supports parsing and printing a multi-character symbol as if it were a punctuation token.
- [parenthesized](https://docs.rs/macro.parenthesized.html)- `parsing`
- Parse a set of parentheses and expose their content to subsequent parsers.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/macro.parse_macro_input.html)- macro_ - input - `parsing`and- `proc-macro`
- Parse the input TokenStream of a macro, triggering a compile error if the tokens fail to parse.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/macro.parse_quote.html)- quote - `parsing`and- `printing`
- Quasi-quotation macro that accepts input like the `quote!`
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/macro.parse_quote_spanned.html)- quote_ - spanned - `parsing`and- `printing`
- This macro is `parse_quote!``quote_spanned!`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Abi](https://docs.rs/struct.Abi.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- The binary interface of a function: `extern "C"`.
- [Angle](https://docs.rs/struct.AngleBracketedGenericArguments.html)- Bracketed - Generic - Arguments - `derive`or- `full`
- Angle bracketed arguments of a path segment: the `<K, V>`in`HashMap<K, V>`.
- [Arm](https://docs.rs/struct.Arm.html)- `full`
- One arm of a `match`expression:`0..=10 => { return true; }`.
- [Assoc](https://docs.rs/struct.AssocConst.html)- Const - `derive`or- `full`
- An equality constraint on an associated constant: the `PANIC = false`in`Trait<PANIC = false>`.
- [Assoc](https://docs.rs/struct.AssocType.html)- Type - `derive`or- `full`
- A binding (equality constraint) on an associated type: the `Item = u8`in`Iterator<Item = u8>`.
- [Attribute](https://docs.rs/struct.Attribute.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- An attribute, like `#[repr(transparent)]`.
- [Bare](https://docs.rs/struct.BareFnArg.html)- FnArg - `derive`or- `full`
- An argument in a function type: the `usize`in`fn(usize) -> bool`.
- [Bare](https://docs.rs/struct.BareVariadic.html)- Variadic - `derive`or- `full`
- The variadic argument of a function pointer like `fn(usize, ...)`.
- [Block](https://docs.rs/struct.Block.html)- `full`
- A braced block containing Rust statements.
- [Bound](https://docs.rs/struct.BoundLifetimes.html)- Lifetimes - `derive`or- `full`
- A set of bound lifetimes: `for<'a, 'b, 'c>`.
- [Const](https://docs.rs/struct.ConstParam.html)- Param - `derive`or- `full`
- A const generic parameter: `const LENGTH: usize`.
- [Constraint](https://docs.rs/struct.Constraint.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- An associated type bound: `Iterator<Item: Display>`.
- [Data](https://docs.rs/struct.DataEnum.html)- Enum - `derive`
- An enum input to a `proc_macro_derive`macro.
- [Data](https://docs.rs/struct.DataStruct.html)- Struct - `derive`
- A struct input to a `proc_macro_derive`macro.
- [Data](https://docs.rs/struct.DataUnion.html)- Union - `derive`
- An untagged union input to a `proc_macro_derive`macro.
- [Derive](https://docs.rs/struct.DeriveInput.html)- Input - `derive`
- Data structure sent to a `proc_macro_derive`macro.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)
- Error returned when a Syn parser cannot parse the input tokens.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprArray.html)- Array - `full`
- A slice literal expression: `[a, b, c, d]`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprAssign.html)- Assign - `full`
- An assignment expression: `a = compute()`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprAsync.html)- Async - `full`
- An async block: `async { ... }`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprAwait.html)- Await - `full`
- An await expression: `fut.await`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprBinary.html)- Binary - `derive`or- `full`
- A binary operation: `a + b`,`a += b`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprBlock.html)- Block - `full`
- A blocked scope: `{ ... }`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprBreak.html)- Break - `full`
- A `break`, with an optional label to break and an optional expression.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprCall.html)- Call - `derive`or- `full`
- A function call expression: `invoke(a, b)`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprCast.html)- Cast - `derive`or- `full`
- A cast expression: `foo as f64`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprClosure.html)- Closure - `full`
- A closure expression: `|a, b| a + b`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprConst.html)- Const - `full`
- A const block: `const { ... }`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprContinue.html)- Continue - `full`
- A `continue`, with an optional label.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprField.html)- Field - `derive`or- `full`
- Access of a named struct field (`obj.k`) or unnamed tuple struct field (`obj.0`).
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprForLoop.html)- ForLoop - `full`
- A for loop: `for pat in expr { ... }`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprGroup.html)- Group - `full`
- An expression contained within invisible delimiters.
- [ExprIf](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprIf.html)- `full`
- An `if`expression with an optional`else`block:`if expr { ... } else { ... }`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprIndex.html)- Index - `derive`or- `full`
- A square bracketed indexing expression: `vector[2]`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprInfer.html)- Infer - `full`
- The inferred value of a const generic argument, denoted `_`.
- [ExprLet](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprLet.html)- `full`
- A `let`guard:`let Some(x) = opt`.
- [ExprLit](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprLit.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- A literal in place of an expression: `1`,`"foo"`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprLoop.html)- Loop - `full`
- Conditionless loop: `loop { ... }`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprMacro.html)- Macro - `derive`or- `full`
- A macro invocation expression: `format!("{}", q)`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprMatch.html)- Match - `full`
- A `match`expression:`match n { Some(n) => {}, None => {} }`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprMethodCall.html)- Method - Call - `derive`or- `full`
- A method call expression: `x.foo::<T>(a, b)`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprParen.html)- Paren - `derive`or- `full`
- A parenthesized expression: `(a + b)`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprPath.html)- Path - `derive`or- `full`
- A path like `core::mem::replace`possibly containing generic parameters and a qualified self-type.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprRange.html)- Range - `full`
- A range expression: `1..2`,`1..`,`..2`,`1..=2`,`..=2`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprRawAddr.html)- RawAddr - `full`
- Address-of operation: `&raw const place`or`&raw mut place`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprReference.html)- Reference - `derive`or- `full`
- A referencing operation: `&a`or`&mut a`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprRepeat.html)- Repeat - `full`
- An array literal constructed from one repeated element: `[0u8; N]`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprReturn.html)- Return - `full`
- A `return`, with an optional value to be returned.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprStruct.html)- Struct - `derive`or- `full`
- A struct literal expression: `Point { x: 1, y: 1 }`.
- [ExprTry](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprTry.html)- `full`
- A try-expression: `expr?`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprTryBlock.html)- TryBlock - `full`
- A try block: `try { ... }`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprTuple.html)- Tuple - `full`
- A tuple expression: `(a, b, c, d)`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprUnary.html)- Unary - `derive`or- `full`
- A unary operation: `!x`,`*x`,`-x`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprUnsafe.html)- Unsafe - `full`
- An unsafe block: `unsafe { ... }`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprWhile.html)- While - `full`
- A while loop: `while expr { ... }`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprYield.html)- Yield - `full`
- A yield expression: `yield expr`.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.Field.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- A field of a struct or enum variant.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldPat.html)- Pat - `full`
- A single field in a struct pattern.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldValue.html)- Value - `derive`or- `full`
- A field-value pair in a struct literal.
- [Fields](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldsNamed.html)- Named - `derive`or- `full`
- Named fields of a struct or struct variant such as `Point { x: f64, y: f64 }`.
- [Fields](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldsUnnamed.html)- Unnamed - `derive`or- `full`
- Unnamed fields of a tuple struct or tuple variant such as `Some(T)`.
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.File.html)- `full`
- A complete file of Rust source code.
- [Foreign](https://docs.rs/struct.ForeignItemFn.html)- Item - Fn - `full`
- A foreign function in an `extern`block.
- [Foreign](https://docs.rs/struct.ForeignItemMacro.html)- Item - Macro - `full`
- A macro invocation within an extern block.
- [Foreign](https://docs.rs/struct.ForeignItemStatic.html)- Item - Static - `full`
- A foreign static item in an `extern`block:`static ext: u8`.
- [Foreign](https://docs.rs/struct.ForeignItemType.html)- Item - Type - `full`
- A foreign type in an `extern`block:`type void`.
- [Generics](https://docs.rs/struct.Generics.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- Lifetimes and type parameters attached to a declaration of a function, enum, trait, etc.
- [Ident](https://docs.rs/struct.Ident.html)
- A word of Rust code, which may be a keyword or legal variable name.
- [Impl](https://docs.rs/struct.ImplGenerics.html)- Generics - `printing`and (- `derive`or- `full`)
- Returned by `Generics::split_for_impl`.
- [Impl](https://docs.rs/struct.ImplItemConst.html)- Item - Const - `full`
- An associated constant within an impl block.
- [Impl](https://docs.rs/struct.ImplItemFn.html)- Item - Fn - `full`
- An associated function within an impl block.
- [Impl](https://docs.rs/struct.ImplItemMacro.html)- Item - Macro - `full`
- A macro invocation within an impl block.
- [Impl](https://docs.rs/struct.ImplItemType.html)- Item - Type - `full`
- An associated type within an impl block.
- [Index](https://docs.rs/struct.Index.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- The index of an unnamed tuple struct field.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemConst.html)- Const - `full`
- A constant item: `const MAX: u16 = 65535`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemEnum.html)- Enum - `full`
- An enum definition: `enum Foo<A, B> { A(A), B(B) }`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemExternCrate.html)- Extern - Crate - `full`
- An `extern crate`item:`extern crate serde`.
- [ItemFn](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemFn.html)- `full`
- A free-standing function: `fn process(n: usize) -> Result<()> { ... }`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemForeignMod.html)- Foreign - Mod - `full`
- A block of foreign items: `extern "C" { ... }`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemImpl.html)- Impl - `full`
- An impl block providing trait or associated items: `impl<A> Trait for Data<A> { ... }`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemMacro.html)- Macro - `full`
- A macro invocation, which includes `macro_rules!`definitions.
- [ItemMod](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemMod.html)- `full`
- A module or module declaration: `mod m`or`mod m { ... }`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemStatic.html)- Static - `full`
- A static item: `static BIKE: Shed = Shed(42)`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemStruct.html)- Struct - `full`
- A struct definition: `struct Foo<A> { x: A }`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemTrait.html)- Trait - `full`
- A trait definition: `pub trait Iterator { ... }`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemTraitAlias.html)- Trait - Alias - `full`
- A trait alias: `pub trait SharableIterator = Iterator + Sync`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemType.html)- Type - `full`
- A type alias: `type Result<T> = core::result::Result<T, MyError>`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemUnion.html)- Union - `full`
- A union definition: `union Foo<A, B> { x: A, y: B }`.
- [ItemUse](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemUse.html)- `full`
- A use declaration: `use alloc::collections::HashMap`.
- [Label](https://docs.rs/struct.Label.html)- `full`
- A lifetime labeling a `for`,`while`, or`loop`.
- [Lifetime](https://docs.rs/struct.Lifetime.html)
- A Rust lifetime: `'a`.
- [Lifetime](https://docs.rs/struct.LifetimeParam.html)- Param - `derive`or- `full`
- A lifetime definition: `'a: 'b + 'c + 'd`.
- [LitBool](https://docs.rs/struct.LitBool.html)
- A boolean literal: `true`or`false`.
- [LitByte](https://docs.rs/struct.LitByte.html)
- A byte literal: `b'f'`.
- [LitByte](https://docs.rs/struct.LitByteStr.html)- Str
- A byte string literal: `b"foo"`.
- [LitCStr](https://docs.rs/struct.LitCStr.html)
- A nul-terminated C-string literal: `c"foo"`.
- [LitChar](https://docs.rs/struct.LitChar.html)
- A character literal: `'a'`.
- [LitFloat](https://docs.rs/struct.LitFloat.html)
- A floating point literal: `1f64`or`1.0e10f64`.
- [LitInt](https://docs.rs/struct.LitInt.html)
- An integer literal: `1`or`1u16`.
- [LitStr](https://docs.rs/struct.LitStr.html)
- A UTF-8 string literal: `"foo"`.
- [Local](https://docs.rs/struct.Local.html)- `full`
- A local `let`binding:`let x: u64 = s.parse()?;`.
- [Local](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalInit.html)- Init - `full`
- The expression assigned in a local `let`binding, including optional diverging`else`block.
- [Macro](https://docs.rs/struct.Macro.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- A macro invocation: `println!("{}", mac)`.
- [Meta](https://docs.rs/struct.MetaList.html)- List - `derive`or- `full`
- A structured list within an attribute, like `derive(Copy, Clone)`.
- [Meta](https://docs.rs/struct.MetaNameValue.html)- Name - Value - `derive`or- `full`
- A name-value pair within an attribute, like `feature = "nightly"`.
- [Parenthesized](https://docs.rs/struct.ParenthesizedGenericArguments.html)- Generic - Arguments - `derive`or- `full`
- Arguments of a function path segment: the `(A, B) -> C`in`Fn(A,B) -> C`.
- [PatConst](https://docs.rs/struct.PatConst.html)- `full`
- A const block: `const { ... }`.
- [PatIdent](https://docs.rs/struct.PatIdent.html)- `full`
- A pattern that binds a new variable: `ref mut binding @ SUBPATTERN`.
- [PatLit](https://docs.rs/struct.PatLit.html)- `full`
- A literal in place of an expression: `1`,`"foo"`.
- [PatMacro](https://docs.rs/struct.PatMacro.html)- `full`
- A macro invocation expression: `format!("{}", q)`.
- [PatOr](https://docs.rs/struct.PatOr.html)- `full`
- A pattern that matches any one of a set of cases.
- [PatParen](https://docs.rs/struct.PatParen.html)- `full`
- A parenthesized pattern: `(A | B)`.
- [PatPath](https://docs.rs/struct.PatPath.html)- `full`
- A path like `core::mem::replace`possibly containing generic parameters and a qualified self-type.
- [PatRange](https://docs.rs/struct.PatRange.html)- `full`

- A reference pattern: `&mut var`.
- [PatRest](https://docs.rs/struct.PatRest.html)- `full`
- The dots in a tuple or slice pattern: `[0, 1, ..]`.
- [PatSlice](https://docs.rs/struct.PatSlice.html)- `full`

- [PatStruct](https://docs.rs/struct.PatStruct.html)- `full`
- A struct or struct variant pattern: `Variant { x, y, .. }`.
- [PatTuple](https://docs.rs/struct.PatTuple.html)- `full`
- A tuple pattern: `(a, b)`.
- [PatTuple](https://docs.rs/struct.PatTupleStruct.html)- Struct - `full`
- A tuple struct or tuple variant pattern: `Variant(x, y, .., z)`.
- [PatType](https://docs.rs/struct.PatType.html)- `full`
- A type ascription pattern: `foo: f64`.
- [PatWild](https://docs.rs/struct.PatWild.html)- `full`

- [Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- A path at which a named item is exported (e.g. `alloc::collections::HashMap`).
- [Path](https://docs.rs/struct.PathSegment.html)- Segment - `derive`or- `full`

- [Precise](https://docs.rs/struct.PreciseCapture.html)- Capture - `full`

- [Predicate](https://docs.rs/struct.PredicateLifetime.html)- Lifetime - `derive`or- `full`

- [Predicate](https://docs.rs/struct.PredicateType.html)- Type - `derive`or- `full`

- [QSelf](https://docs.rs/struct.QSelf.html)- `derive`or- `full`

- [Receiver](https://docs.rs/struct.Receiver.html)- `full`
- The `self`argument of an associated method.
- [Signature](https://docs.rs/struct.Signature.html)- `full`
- A function signature in a trait or implementation: `unsafe fn initialize(&self)`.
- [Stmt](https://docs.rs/struct.StmtMacro.html)- Macro - `full`
- A macro invocation in statement position.
- [Trait](https://docs.rs/struct.TraitBound.html)- Bound - `derive`or- `full`

- [Turbofish](https://docs.rs/struct.Turbofish.html)- `printing`and (- `derive`or- `full`)

- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeArray.html)- Array - `derive`or- `full`

- An `impl Bound1 + Bound2 + Bound3`type where`Bound`is a trait or a lifetime.

- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeReference.html)- Reference - `derive`or- `full`
- A reference type: `&'a T`or`&'a mut T`.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeSlice.html)- Slice - `derive`or- `full`

- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeTraitObject.html)- Trait - Object - `derive`or- `full`

- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeTuple.html)- Tuple - `derive`or- `full`

- [UseGlob](https://docs.rs/struct.UseGlob.html)- `full`
- A glob import in a `use`item:`*`.
- [UseGroup](https://docs.rs/struct.UseGroup.html)- `full`

- [UsePath](https://docs.rs/struct.UsePath.html)- `full`

- [UseRename](https://docs.rs/struct.UseRename.html)- `full`

# bincode - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bincode/^1.3.3/

## Expand description

Bincode is a crate for encoding and decoding using a tiny binary serialization strategy. Using it, you can easily go from having an object in memory, quickly serialize it to bytes, and then deserialize it back just as fast!

[§](https://docs.rs#using-basic-functions)Using Basic Functions

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
fn main() {
    // The object that we will serialize.
    let target: Option<String>  = Some("hello world".to_string());
    let encoded: Vec<u8> = bincode::serialize(&target).unwrap();
    let decoded: Option<String> = bincode::deserialize(&encoded[..]).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(target, decoded);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#128bit-numbers)128bit numbers

Support for `i128` and `u128` is automatically enabled on Rust toolchains
greater than or equal to `1.26.0` and disabled for targets which do not support it

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use config::`- [Config](https://docs.rs/config/struct.Config.html);- Deprecated
- `pub use config::`- [DefaultOptions](https://docs.rs/config/struct.DefaultOptions.html);
- `pub use config::`- [Options](https://docs.rs/config/trait.Options.html);
- `pub use de::read::`- [BincodeRead](https://docs.rs/de/read/trait.BincodeRead.html);
- `pub use de::`- [Deserializer](https://docs.rs/de/struct.Deserializer.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [config](https://docs.rs/config/index.html)
- `bincode`uses a Builder-pattern to configure the Serializers and Deserializers in this crate. This means that if you need to customize the behavior of- `bincode`, you should create an instance of the- `DefaultOptions`struct:
- [de](https://docs.rs/de/index.html)
- Deserialize bincode data to a Rust data structure.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Serializer](https://docs.rs/struct.Serializer.html)
- An Serializer that encodes values directly into a Writer.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.ErrorKind.html)- Kind
- The kind of error that can be produced during a serialization or deserialization.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [config](https://docs.rs/fn.config.html)- Deprecated
- Get a default configuration object.
- [deserialize](https://docs.rs/fn.deserialize.html)
- Deserializes a slice of bytes into an instance of `T`using the default configuration.
- [deserialize_](https://docs.rs/fn.deserialize_from.html)- from
- Deserializes an object directly from a `Read`er using the default configuration.
- [deserialize_](https://docs.rs/fn.deserialize_from_custom.html)- from_ - custom
- Deserializes an object from a custom `BincodeRead`er using the default configuration. It is highly recommended to use`deserialize_from`unless you need to implement`BincodeRead`for performance reasons.
- [options](https://docs.rs/fn.options.html)
- Get a default configuration object.
- [serialize](https://docs.rs/fn.serialize.html)
- Serializes a serializable object into a `Vec`of bytes using the default configuration.
- [serialize_](https://docs.rs/fn.serialize_into.html)- into
- Serializes an object directly into a `Writer`using the default configuration.
- [serialized_](https://docs.rs/fn.serialized_size.html)- size
- Returns the size that an object would be if serialized using Bincode with the default configuration.

# serde_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/serde_core/^1.0.226/

## Expand description

Serde is a framework for * ser*ializing and

*serializing Rust data structures efficiently and generically.*

**de**The `serde_core` crate contains Serde’s trait definitions with **no support
for #[derive()]**.

In crates that derive an implementation of `Serialize` or `Deserialize`, you
must depend on the [ serde](https://crates.io/crates/serde) crate, not

`serde_core`.In crates that handwrite implementations of Serde traits, or only use them
as trait bounds, depending on `serde_core` is permitted. But `serde`
re-exports all of these traits and can be used for this use case too. If in
doubt, disregard `serde_core` and always use `serde`.

Crates that depend on `serde_core` instead of `serde` are able to compile in
parallel with `serde_derive` even when `serde`’s “derive” feature is turned on,
as shown in the following build timings.

| When `serde_json`depends on`serde` |

| When `serde_json`depends on`serde_core` |

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [de](https://docs.rs/de/index.html)
- Generic data structure deserialization framework.
- [ser](https://docs.rs/ser/index.html)
- Generic data structure serialization framework.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [forward_](https://docs.rs/macro.forward_to_deserialize_any.html)- to_ - deserialize_ - any
- Helper macro when implementing the `Deserializer`part of a new data format for Serde.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Deserialize](https://docs.rs/trait.Deserialize.html)
- A **data structure**that can be deserialized from any data format supported by Serde.
- [Deserializer](https://docs.rs/trait.Deserializer.html)
- A **data format**that can deserialize any data structure supported by Serde.
- [Serialize](https://docs.rs/trait.Serialize.html)
- A **data structure**that can be serialized into any data format supported by Serde.
- [Serializer](https://docs.rs/trait.Serializer.html)
- A **data format**that can serialize any data structure supported by Serde.

# solana_address - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/solana-address/^2.2.0/

## Expand description

Address representation for Solana.

An address is a sequence of 32 bytes, often shown as a base58 encoded string (e.g. 14grJpemFaf88c8tiVb77W7TYg2W3ir6pfkKz3YjhhZ5).

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [address](https://docs.rs/macro.address.html)- `decode`
- Convenience macro to define a static `Address`value.
- [declare_](https://docs.rs/macro.declare_deprecated_id.html)- deprecated_ - id - `decode`
- Same as `declare_id`
- [declare_](https://docs.rs/macro.declare_id.html)- id - `decode`
- Convenience macro to declare a static address and functions to interact with it.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Address](https://docs.rs/struct.Address.html)
- The address of a [Solana account](https://solana.com/docs/core/accounts).
- [Address](https://docs.rs/struct.AddressHasher.html)- Hasher - `rand`and neither- `target_os=solana`nor BPF
- A faster, but less collision resistant hasher for addresses.
- [Address](https://docs.rs/struct.AddressHasherBuilder.html)- Hasher - Builder - `rand`and neither- `target_os=solana`nor BPF
- A builder for faster, but less collision resistant hasher for addresses.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [ADDRESS_](https://docs.rs/constant.ADDRESS_BYTES.html)- BYTES
- Number of bytes in an address.
- [MAX_](https://docs.rs/constant.MAX_SEEDS.html)- SEEDS
- Maximum number of seeds
- [MAX_](https://docs.rs/constant.MAX_SEED_LEN.html)- SEED_ - LEN
- maximum length of derived `Address`seed
- [PDA_](https://docs.rs/constant.PDA_MARKER.html)- MARKER - Non-BPF
- Marker used to find program derived addresses (PDAs).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [address_](https://docs.rs/fn.address_eq.html)- eq
- Custom implementation of equality for `Address`.
- [bytes_](https://docs.rs/fn.bytes_are_curve_point.html)- are_ - curve_ - point - `curve25519`or- `syscalls`
- Check whether the given bytes represent a valid curve point.

    &self,

Resize the account’s data: Either truncating or zero extending.

Note:  Account data can be increased within a single call by up to
`solana_program::entrypoint::MAX_PERMITTED_DATA_INCREASE` bytes.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety-1)Safety

This method makes assumptions about the layout and location of memory
referenced by `AccountInfo` fields. It should only be called for
instances of `AccountInfo` that were created by the runtime and received
in the `process_instruction` entrypoint of a program.
